text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President of Finland Martti Ahtisaari paid a one-day visit to Tallinn, opening the renovated building of the Finnish embassy and discussing security in the Baltic sea region with Estonian President Lennart Meri.
- Police are looking for Imre Perli, a former employee of a mobile phone company, who is suspected to have leaked a secret data base to the black market.

- The government approved amendments to the criminal code, adding a 25-year and a life-term prison sentence to the current maximum imprisonment of 15 years. The new sentences are aimed at providing an alternative to the death sentence, which Estonia would like to scrap.
- Twelve defence force conscripts who are Jehovah's Witnesses, are allowed to carry out their duty in alternative service in the Tallinn rescue company.
- The Nordic countries support Estonia's aims to be among the first new member-countries of NATO, the prime ministers of Iceland and Denmark said at a Copenhagen Nordic Council summit.
- A 228-metre long tanker, Protank Orinoko, that arrived in Tallinn's Muuga port is the largest vessel to visit Estonia.
- The tax department has compiled a black list of firms suspected of sales tax evasions and plans to carry out a large-scale inspection.
